clue.text: Drink cures heart failure

indicators.note: a heart failure suggests the words cures heart breaking down, so their letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A drink claimed to remedy cardiac trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' reorders the ten letters of CURES HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Cuba's leader a revolutionary sort

indicators.note: the leader of the word Cuba's is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the word sort being turned over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cuba's head of state was a rebel by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: C (Cuba's leader) and A are followed by SORT rearranged ('revolutionary') to give STRO; the whole clue also describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution and then governed the island for decades.

clue.text: Jack's training for the fifteen? That's sudden!

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman)
a rugby union team has fifteen players, and Rugby Union is abbreviated RU
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A sailor doing fitness work for the rugby team, and it happened all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: RUGBY UNION (RU) is the fifteen-a-side code of rugby football, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt is a synonym of sudden, describing something that happens without warning.

clue.text: The best soft drink featured on TV?

definitions.text: The best soft drink featured on TV?

parts.words: The best soft drink featured on TV?
parts.note: read literally, the finest of the fizzy drinks; really the name of a long-running BBC television music chart show

explanation.surface: Which fizzy drink comes out top when advertised on television?
explanation.walkthrough: The show was a weekly BBC programme presenting the best-selling records; POPS also means fizzy soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the BBC chart programme and literally means the leader among fizzy beverages.

clue.text: They may look right to superiors

definitions.text: They may look right to superiors

parts.words: They may look right to superiors
parts.note: the military command 'right!' turns soldiers' gaze towards a saluting officer as they march past

explanation.surface: Things that seem correct to those higher up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look right' suggests seeming correct; the parade-ground order makes the organs of sight literally turn right.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade the order to turn the head makes soldiers' organs of vision face the reviewing officer.

clue.text: Special outfits for round-the-world trips?

parts.note: a journey around the world suggests travel by sea or air, but here it means orbiting the planet in a spacecraft

explanation.surface: Clothing designed for a global tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round-the-world' suggests a gap-year tour; an astronaut in orbit travels round the world too.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts wear pressurised protective garments when travelling in orbit around the Earth.

clue.text: Huts need to be built just so

indicators.note: building means putting the letters of huts together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sheds have to be constructed exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to be built' rearranges HUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this way or in this manner, as just so does.

clue.text: Crashed pilot has treatment provided here

indicators.note: a crashed plane is wrecked, so the letters of pilot has are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An airman who came down is being given medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' rearranges PILOTHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where patients receive medical care is the definition of an infirmary.

clue.text: Whales have been known to be beached and abandoned

definitions.text: Whales have been known to be beached

explanation.surface: Whales sometimes end up on the shore, left to die.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a whole phrase: whales that are beached are said to be stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: A beached whale is left high and dry on the shore, and someone abandoned is left helpless without means to go on.

clue.text: Broken lamp recast in waste material

indicators.note: broken suggests the words lamp recast being smashed and their letters put back together differently

explanation.surface: A broken lamp gets remade from rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recast' looks like the anagram signal, but 'Broken' is: it rearranges LAMP RECAST, ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded iron, steel and other metals collected for recycling.

clue.text: Employer in serious error

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words serious error, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A boss has made a grave mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across seriOUS ERror.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs something makes use of it, a sense of the definition here as a noun for someone using a thing.

clue.text: Painter calling home, possibly about the start of employment

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
possibly signals that the words calling home may be rearranged into another order
the start of the word employment is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An artist phones his family, perhaps about a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CALLING HOME, and 'about' wraps those letters round E, the start of employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo was the Italian Renaissance artist who decorated the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

clue.text: Quickly remove label showing exorbitant price

explanation.surface: Tear off a sticker that shows an outrageous cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'label showing' is linking matter: the surface pictures stripping off a price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip off is to tear away fast, and as a noun the phrase means a swindle where someone is grossly overcharged.

clue.text: Mockery is the cause of Ironside's confusion

indicators.note: confusion suggests the letters of Ironside are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Ridicule is what bewilders Ironside, the TV detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letters: 'confusion' rearranges IRONSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is scornful ridicule, the same as mockery.

clue.text: Effect a change of tack at sea

definitions.text: a change of tack at sea

explanation.surface: Cause a sailing boat to switch direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about is to cause or achieve something, and in sailing it means to turn a vessel onto the opposite tack.

clue.text: Full board in a way

parts.note: thorough means complete or full
board means meals provided, as in bed and board, which is fare

explanation.surface: Complete meals provided while on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is food here, as in 'full board' at a hotel, not a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a road or public route, a kind of street.

clue.text: Blissfully unaware

parts.note: echoes the proverb that ignorance is bliss: someone happy because they lack knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking knowledge of something is uninformed, and the proverb says such a state is bliss.

clue.text: Sibyl involved with ECO transport

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of Sibyl entangled with the three capitals that follow to make a new word

parts.note: the capitals as held read ECO, but the anagram needs E, C, C

explanation.surface: A woman named Sibyl is engaged in green travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges SIBYL plus ECC; the clue as held shows ECO, a slip, since only ECC gives the second C the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicycles are pedal-powered two-wheelers, a means of getting about.

clue.text: Not necessarily a story associated with vice

definitions.text: Not necessarily a story associated with vice

parts.words: Not necessarily a story associated with vice
parts.note: vice suggests wickedness, but a vice is also the workshop clamp that holds things tight; a clamping yarn need not be a sordid one

explanation.surface: A tale that isn't always about crime and sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice' as depravity is the false path; the clamp holds firmly, as an exciting story holds a reader.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciting narrative that holds a reader's attention is described as gripping.

clue.text: John, half-gone on the bottle, is jolly

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next
half of the name John has gone, leaving its first two letters

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: John, half-drunk, is merry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-gone' and 'on the bottle' paint a drinker; in a down clue 'on' stacks the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and good-humoured, a synonym of merry.

clue.text: He's lawless-a little grasping also

indicators.note: grasping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a little means a bit
also means and

explanation.surface: An outlaw who is also a little greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' looks like greed in the surface but is the container signal, the little piece holding the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber living outside the law.

clue.text: Games period

explanation.surface: Sporting contests held over a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympiad is a celebration of the Olympic Games, and also the four-year interval between them.

clue.text: Breed of goats originating from Aragon

indicators.note: originating from suggests the new word is made out of the letters of Aragon rearranged

explanation.surface: Goats bred in the Spanish region of Aragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originating from' rearranges ARAGON; Aragon is a region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a goat breed from Turkey whose wool is called mohair.

clue.text: Being old, agreed about being dropped

indicators.note: being dropped means the following piece is removed from the word agreed

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Elderly, accepted terms about to be abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being dropped' takes RE out of AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, describing someone who has lived many years.

clue.text: A lonely one lacking a supporter

indicators.note: lacking means the word lonely is without the letters of the next piece

parts.note: taken as written: the letters O, N, E

explanation.surface: A solitary person without anyone to back them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lonely one' reads as a solitary person; 'lacking' strips three letters spelled out by the clue word one, and the final 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a friend or partner who backs you up.

clue.text: Utterly restricted

parts.note: utterly seems to mean completely, but here it means in uttering: limited in what one can say

explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to speak through shyness or nerves is limited in their speech.

clue.text: Paper match

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination paper, and in cricket a Test is an international match.

clue.text: Part of the film scenery that may be rented out

explanation.surface: A piece of a movie set that could be let.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLAT is a painted panel of stage or studio scenery; a STUDIO FLAT is the British name for a one-room apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted scenery panel in a film studio is a flat, and a one-room bedsit apartment is a common rental.
